records.c: The morph's frame in its form's set of shapes, from the animation sequence.
The morph's X across the course: sub-pixels ($1F01), pixels ($1F02) and the high byte ($1F03).
X's low byte.
X's high byte.
The morph's height: sub-pixels ($1F04) and pixels ($1F05), 0 at the top of the view.
The height, pixels.
A byte cleared at each run and read by nothing.
The morph's speed across, signed: positive to the right.
The morph's speed up or down, 16 bits ($1F09 the high byte), positive downwards.
The speed up or down, high byte.
The Jumper's spring and the Flyer's climb, built up while the button is held.
The Runner's stride: how far each frame of its stride moves it.
$FF while the morph stands on something.
The edges of the view the morph has passed, with bit 7 set: 1 the top, 2 the bottom, 4 the left, 8 the right; the next screen is drawn ($253E).
The Runner's and the Flyer's power, built up by moving the stick (as Head Throwing's run-up) or by holding the button, up to $7F.
Gravity, taken off the Flyer's power ($1F0E) when it flies.
The fastest the morph may fall or climb.
The Burrower's state: bit 7 digging, bit 6 the direction.
$FF while the power ($1F0E) builds and drains (Runner and Jumper).
$FF while the run is under way: the frame handler moves the morph.
The view's left edge on the course map, in tiles.
The view's top edge on the course map, in tiles.
Two bytes nothing reads.
Frames to the animation's next step.
$FF when the animation's next step is due.
The animation's rate: frames a step.
The morph's state: 0 the blob, 1 changing into a form, 2 changing back, 3 the Flyer, 4 the Runner, 5 the Burrower, 6 the Jumper, 7 out of energy, 8 gone.
The form the morph becomes when the change is over.
The form's set of shapes: 0 the blob, 1 the Flyer, 2 the Runner, 3 the Burrower, 4 the Jumper, 5 out of energy.
The animation sequence the new form starts with.
$FF when the energy has run out; bit 6 when the run is over.
The energy, 16 bits, $03FF full: four bars of $100 ($1F20 the bar, $1F1F the level within it).
The energy's bar, 0 to 3.
draw_energy's level and bar ($1F22), the last drawn.
The bar drawn last.
Frames to the next drain of energy, 20.
Frames to the clock's next second, 50.
A byte nothing reads.
The run's time in BCD: seconds ($1F26) and minutes ($1F27).
The minutes.
Four bytes cleared with the clock and read by nothing.
Cleared with the clock, the second of the four.
Cleared with the clock, the third of the four.
Cleared with the clock, the last of the four.
$01 at the start, $FF once the clock has passed 70 seconds; read by nothing.
Cleared at each run like $1F06, and also read by nothing.
$FF while the Jumper is crouched to spring.
$FF once the Jumper has sprung ($29AC), and still after it lands, until DOWN crouches it again ($2A03, back to 0); change_back sets it too ($2A5D).
$FF when the morph has just been hurt.
$FF when the morph has reached a power pill.
$FF when the pill's sprites are to be taken off.
The morph's tile on the map: across ($1F33) and down ($1F34).
The morph's tile down.
$FF when the morph has crossed the finish ($80 when the demo runs out).
Frames left of a nudge across after hitting a wall (bit 7 to the left).
A byte nothing reads.
$FF in the demo.
The demo's frames to its next step (5) and the current entry's steps left ($1F3A).
The demo entry's steps left.
The demo's steps left, 100.
$FF while a demo entry sets the power ($1F3D) instead of the stick.
The power a demo entry sets.
Six bytes nothing reads.
$FF while a run is under way: energy drains and the speed decays.
$FF when the view has wrapped round the course map's right end.
The Jumper's speed across while it springs.
The controls, a 0 bit for each held: up (bit 0), down (1), left (2), right (3), fire (4).
The last of LEFT and RIGHT pressed, for the power.
The first shape of the form's set ($346B).

The eleven animation sequences, lists of frames (pairs of frame and stride for the Runner), ended by $FF: 0 the blob, 1 changing into a form, 2 changing back, 3 the Flyer, 4 and 5 the Runner, 6 the Burrower digging, 7 the Jumper crouching, 8 the Jumper springing, 9 out of energy, 10 gone.
Sequence 0, the blob: frames 0 and 1.
Sequence 1, changing into a form: 00 01, ended by $FF.
Sequence 2, changing back: 01 00, ended by $FF.
Sequence 3, the Flyer: 02 03 04 05, ended by $FF.
Sequence 4, the Runner (frame and stride pairs): 04 09 05 04 06 04 07 06 08 03, ended by $FF.
A byte between sequences 4 and 5 that nothing reads.
Sequence 5, the Runner's second (frame and stride pairs): 09 0B 0A 04 0B 04 02 06 03 04, ended by $FF.
A byte between sequences 5 and 6 that nothing reads.
Sequence 6, the Burrower digging: 02 03 04 05 04 03, ended by $FF.
Sequence 7, the Jumper crouching: 02 03 04 05, ended by $FF.
Sequence 8, the Jumper springing: 05 04 03 02, ended by $FF.
Sequence 9, running out of energy: 03 00, ended by $FF.
A byte between sequences 9 and 10 that nothing reads.
Sequence 10, gone: 00 01 02, ended by $FF.
The event's entry, from the resident menu's table: shows the event's title screen through the resident $C540 (A = 4, this event).
Sets up the machine ($308E) and turns the screen on.
Left over and called by nothing: a test loop that draws a bar ($33F8) with a rising value and prints it in hex ($399C), for ever.

Copies the course's character set from $8500 to $5000, draws the top panel ($37F5), the panel's form icon ($37A3), the view ($324E), clears the time panel, the clock and the distance, then alternates players: player one, player two, and round again. A run: effect 10, the morph reset ($2B66), waits for the player ($2E8A), starts the form, shows "GO" and runs until the morph finishes or runs out of energy.
Within JSR $3781: the operand's high byte.
After player two, player one again.

The run's loop, once a frame: places the morph's sprites ($3471), waits for the frame, draws the next screen when the morph has passed an edge ($253E), takes a power pill off ($3334), runs the form's controls ($2798), takes a pill ($2E4E), draws the energy, the speed and the jump bars ($33C2, $3381, $3395) and the time; until the finish ($20A4) or out of energy ($209C).
In the demo, fire on any device ends it.
Out of energy: the time panel, "OUT OF ENERGY" (message 9), and the next player.
Finished: waits for the morph's sequence to end, counts the energy left off the time ($25FA), keeps the time if it is the player's best ($306E), "FINISHED" (message 10), and the next player.

Once a frame from the raster interrupt: the sound ($3D85); while the run is under way, the controls (the device's, or the demo's, $268F), and with the run started the energy and the speed ($20F9), gravity ($2114), the move ($2168), the power ($24E7), the clock ($2BF2) and the message line ($365D).
Steps the animation timer, drains the energy ($2B16) and lets the jump's lift fall ($2D9E).
Gravity: on the ground none, otherwise $40 a frame, less what the Flyer's power ($1F0F) holds up, added to the fall speed, which stays between -$70 and $70 and above the form's limit ($1F10).

Moves the morph: a nudge from a wall first ($216D); the Runner's stride, or the speed across x 16, added to X; the fall speed x 16 added to the height; then the walls and floors ($228D) and the view's edges ($2228).
A nudge: four pixels a frame away from the wall until it runs out.

Notes which edges of the view the morph has passed in $1F0D: above row $13 (unless the view is at the map's top, where it stops), below $74, left of X $10 (unless at the map's left end, where it stops) and right of $121.

Finds the morph's tile on the map from its X and height and the view's corner. A tile column $FE or more is the finish ($1F35). Then a power pill on that tile is taken ($1F31). Falling: lands on a solid tile ($24D9 bit 7), setting the height to the tile's top; a fall of $18 or more hurts unless the morph is the Jumper ($24A4), otherwise effect 1. Climbing: stops under a solid tile, hurt the same way. Across: walls stop it, with a nudge back ($1F36); the Burrower digs through tiles whose bit 6 is clear.
Within LDA $1F02: the X halved, its high bit shifted in, less 8, gives the morph's place across in two-pixel steps.
The finish line, map column $FE or more.
A pill on this tile: taken, and wiped from the list.
Landed: the height to the tile's top, on the ground; a fall of $18 or more hurts (($1F09 - $18 + $10) x 4), unless the morph is the Jumper; otherwise effect 1.
Within LDA #$01: effect 1, the landing, on voice 3.
Climbing: off the ground; a solid tile above stops it ($239F).
Hit a ceiling: a climb of $10 or more hurts; the speeds stop and the height goes to the tile's middle.
Not falling: off the ground.
Across: the Runner, or any form moving, checks the tile ahead.
A wall: tiles with bit 6 set stop the Burrower too; a speed of $10 or more hurts, and the morph is nudged back two frames ($1F36).

Moving left: tests the tile in the morph's own column, where check_ahead tests the next. Whether to test the row below as well comes from the X position's low bits ($1F02), no form is let through, and every hit sets the nudge $82 ($249D).
Takes A off the energy (to at least 0) and plays effect 2; the power drops to 0 and $1F30 is set.
Effect 2, the hurt.

Returns the map's byte for tile X, Y (the map is 256 tiles across, a page a row from $8D00), through an LDA whose operand it rewrites; bit 7 solid, bit 6 too hard to dig, the low six bits the tile's picture.
map_tile's LDA operand: the tile's column ($24E4) and its row's page ($24E5).
The row's page: $8D plus the row.

While the power builds ($1F12): the human gains power for each new direction of LEFT or RIGHT after the other, more when slow (4 plus a share of what is left), as in Head Throwing's run-up; in the demo the power moves one a frame towards the entry's ($1F3D). Then it loses 2 a frame.

The morph has passed an edge of the view: effect 12, the run paused, and the view moves on by a screen: 3 tiles up or down (the morph's height moved $61 the other way), or 8 tiles across (the morph's X moved $100), wrapping at the map's right end ($1F45); then redraws the view ($324E).
Within AND #$01: bit 0, the top edge.
Keeps the view's row within the map's 32 rows.
After the finish: the energy left, 8 at a time, comes off the time a second at a time (effect 11, two frames each), until the energy or the time runs out.
The last demo chosen.
The demo: picks one of four recorded runs at random, never the same twice running, and plays it a step every 5 frames for 100 steps.
Plays the demo's next entry when the last has run its steps: its controls, its length in steps, and for the power entries ($20 clear) the power to reach ($1F3D). $FF ends the list.
The four recorded runs.
The recorded runs, from their second byte.
Recorded run 0: entries of controls (inverted), steps, and a power for those without bit 5.
The last byte of the demo's runs.
Starts animation sequence A: points $04/$05 at it, takes its first frame (and the Runner's stride), and resets the animation timer.
When the animation is due, takes the sequence's next frame (and the Runner's stride). Returns carry set at its end.
Runs the morph's state through the JMP at $27AE, from state_table; when the energy has just run out (bit 7 of $1F1E set) it runs energy_gone ($27B1) instead.
The JMP's operand.
The JMP operand's high byte.
Out of energy: the morph changes back and then fails (state 7).

The nine state routines: 0 the blob ($27FF), 1 changing ($28AE), 2 changing back ($2A7D), 3 the Flyer ($28CA), 4 the Runner ($2919), 5 the Burrower ($2A1A), 6 the Jumper ($2972), 7 out of energy ($2A86), 8 gone ($2AA6).
The state routines' addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Back to the blob: its shapes, its sequence at rate $50, state 0, and the speeds stopped.
State 0, the blob: RIGHT changes it to the Runner, LEFT to the Burrower, UP to the Flyer and DOWN to the Jumper (sequence 1 and effect 6 for each); otherwise it wobbles.
RIGHT: the Runner, its shapes (set 2), state 4 to come, the power building.
LEFT: the Burrower, its shapes (set 3), state 5 to come, effect 4.
UP: the Flyer, its shapes (set 1), climbing at most $F0, state 3 to come, the power building.
The change starts: sequence 1 at rate $50, state 1, effect 6.
DOWN: the Jumper, its shapes (set 4), state 6 to come, rate $10, its lift at $30.
State 1: at the end of the change, the new form's sequence and state; the Burrower plays effect 4.
State 3, the Flyer: FIRE changes it back. The power holds it up against gravity; UP keeps the power building, and the frames flap at a rate set by the power ($2ABA).
State 4, the Runner: FIRE changes it back. Its stride comes from the power; on the ground its sequence repeats, with a footstep on frames 2 and 7 (effect 1).

State 6, the Jumper: FIRE changes it back. DOWN crouches it (sequence 7, effect 8) and builds the spring; letting go springs it up by the spring plus the power (sequence 8, effect 9). LEFT and RIGHT steer it at $F0 or $10 while it is in the air.
State 5, the Burrower: FIRE changes it back. On the ground, RIGHT digs on (8 across a frame, sequence 6); it falls when the tile under it gives way.
Changes back towards the blob: sequence 2 at rate $50, state 2, effect 5.
State 2: at the end, the blob ($27D1).
State 7: stops the morph; at the end of its sequence, the out-of-energy shapes (set 5), state 8 and sequence 10.
State 8: at the end of the sequence the morph's sprites go off and the run is over ($1F1E = $C0).
Sets the animation's rate from the power ($2AD6, by power / 4) and, for the Runner, its stride ($2AF6).
The animation's rates by power / 4: $7F standing, down to $10 at full power.
The Runner's strides by power / 4: 0 to $50.
Every 20 frames, takes the form's cost ($2B5F) off the energy; at 0 the energy has run out ($1F1E).
Out of energy.
The energy each state costs every 20 frames: the blob and the changes nothing, the Flyer 3, the Runner 1, the Burrower 8, the Jumper 2.

Resets a run: energy $03FF, the speeds, flags and forms cleared, the view at the map's top left (row $15, column 0), the morph at X $30, height $50, and one of the two lists of power pills, chosen at random, copied to $2DEE.
$FF while the clock runs.
Every 50 frames adds a second to the clock in BCD, carrying into the minutes at 60, and shows it.
Past 70 seconds: $1F2C.
Clears the clock and its spare bytes.
Sets the clock to 0:00 and shows it.
Starts the clock.
Stops the clock.
The seven-segment patterns of the digits 0 to 9, then six more nothing asks for.
Draws the time as four seven-segment digits at $4064, $4066, $4069 and $406B, with the colon at $4090 and $40B8.
The byte after draw_digit's RTS: 0, read by nothing.
Draws the seven-segment pattern A as a digit two characters wide and three high at the screen address X, Y: each cell's character is $28 plus the segments it shows.
draw_digit's work byte.
Each frame lets the Jumper's lift fall by one; while it crouches, the lift rises one and the power two (to under $7F).
Puts a power pill's sprites on the screen when one of the list's pills lies in the view ($3343).
The sixteen power pills on the course: each a map column and row, $FF once taken.
The pills' rows, interleaved with their columns.
The two lists of pills, 32 bytes each, one of which each run copies.
A power pill: adds $FF to the energy (to at most $03FF), takes the pill's sprites off, and plays effect 7.
Shows "PLAYER ONE (or TWO) PRESS FIRE TO START" and waits up to 256 frames for fire on any device, which becomes the player's ($3705). Then starts the run: "GET READY", 50 frames, "GO".
No fire: if player two was waited for, back to player one; if player one, the demo.
Draws the view, the blob, and places its sprites.
await_player's frame count: 256 frames before the next player's prompt gives up.
The addresses of the 13 messages, numbered from 0. Only 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10 are shown.
The message addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Message 0: empty, $FF alone. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 1, "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 2, "DEMO MODE", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 3, "GAME PAUSED", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 4, "METAMORPH MARATHON", ended by $FF.
Message 5, "PLAYER ONE PRESS FIRE TO START", ended by $FF.
Message 6, "PLAYER TWO PRESS FIRE TO START", ended by $FF.
Message 7, "GET READY", ended by $FF.
Message 8, "GO", ended by $FF.
Message 9, "OUT OF ENERGY", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 10, "FINISHED", ended by $FF.
Message 11, "PRESS ESCAPE TO QUIT.", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Message 12, "STOP TO QUIT   ANY KEY TO CONTINUE", ended by $FF. Nothing in this part shows it.
Each player's best time in this event, in BCD: player one's seconds and minutes ($306A), player two's ($306C); $9999 none yet.
Player one's best, minutes.
Player two's best, seconds.
Player two's best, minutes.
Keeps the run's time ($1F26) as player $29's best when it is lower than the best so far.

Sets up the machine: silences the SID ($3E1C); banks the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out with the I/O in; the NMI to an RTI ($7450) and the IRQ to $311E; the CIA's timer interrupt off and the raster interrupt on at line 256; the VIC to bank 1 ($4000); multicolour text; clears the screen ($31D1); border blue; sprites 0 to 3 and 6 black, 4 and 5 yellow, 7 green and multicolour with red; all sprites off.
The raster interrupt's band, 0 or 1.
The next band's raster line, bit 8 (in bit 7).
The two bands' raster lines and their bit 8: line $71 (the course's top, screen row 8) and line $F2 (below the course).
The raster lines' bit 8, interleaved.
The raster interrupt: counts it ($31B7), saves the registers, and sends a BRK to $0810 ($312D); otherwise jumps to the band's handler through the JMP at $3130.
A BRK: back to the resident code at $0810.
The JMP to the band's handler, its operand set from $3133.
The handler's low byte.
The handler's high byte.
The two bands' handlers: $3137 the course, $3157 the rest.
The handlers' high bytes, interleaved.
Line $71: the course's character set ($5000) and its three colours from $7FFC, $7FFD and $7FFE.

Line $F2: the panel's character set ($4800) and colours (blue, black, light blue) for the message row and the top of the next frame; then the frame's work ($20C7), the cursor's flash ($31B8) and the RUN/STOP check ($7440).
Acknowledges the interrupt and sets up the other band: its raster line and its handler.
Counts raster interrupts, two a frame.
Every 10 frames, inverts character $27, the message's cursor, in the panel's character set ($4939).
flash_cursor's count.
Clears the screen to character 0 with colour RAM 8, the bottom row's colour white, and the multicolours light blue and black.

Takes the pills off ($3334), then draws the view: four rows of ten tiles from the map ($8D00 + the view's row, a page a row, from its column), each through draw_tile ($32D0) from screen row 8 ($4140); then shows a pill in it ($2DCB).
Draws tile A (its low six bits) four characters by four: the 16 characters from $8100 + A x 16, and each one's colour from the table at $8000.
The LDA operand draw_tile points at the tile's characters.
The operand's high byte: $81 plus the tile's high bits.
draw_tile's saved X and Y ($331F).
draw_tile's saved Y.
The 16 cells' screen offsets in a tile: four rows of four, 40 apart.
Takes the pill's sprites (6 and 7) off.
A spare RTS.
Puts the pill's two sprites (6 and 7) on the view's tile at row A and column X, Y = A x 32 + $7A and X = (X x 16 + $12) x 2, and turns them on.
Zeroes the power and draws its bar at $4052, empty, for power x 2.
Draws the power bar at $4052 for the power as it stands, x 2.
Zeroes the morph's tile across ($1F33) and draws the course bar at $40CA for it, empty.
Draws the course bar at $40CA for the morph's tile across as it stands.
Draws the four energy bars full.
fill_energy's bar count.
The four energy bars' screen addresses' low bytes, bar 0 lowest: $40D3, $40AB, $4083 and $405B.
Draws the energy: when its bar has changed since last time, fills the bar left behind full (or empties it), then draws the current bar for the level within it.
Draws a bar of six cells at ($17) for the value A: A less A / 4, over 4 (at most $2F); full cells ($40), one part cell ($39 plus the remainder) and blanks; and colours the six cells red.
draw_bar's level ($345C) and value ($345D).
draw_bar's value.
Sets the form's set of shapes A ($1F1C) and its first shape ($346B), and colours the form's icon in the panel ($37A3).
The first shape of each set: 0 the blob, 2 the Flyer, 8 the Runner, $14 the Burrower, $1A the Jumper, $20 out of energy.

Places the morph's six sprites: 0, 2, 4 and 5 at its X + 8, 1 and 3 another 24 on; 0, 1 and 4 at its height + $5A, 2, 3 and 5 another 16 down; 4 and 5 twice as wide; pointers $60 to $67; then builds the current shape (the set's first + the frame) into them ($34F7, $3543) and turns 0 to 5 on.
Over 255: the high X bits for sprites 0 to 5.
The right-hand sprites (1 and 3) over 255.

Builds shape A's outline, 128 bytes from $5A00 + A x 128, into sprites $60-$63 at $5800: in two halves of five blank rows and sixteen of four bytes, three to the left sprite and one to the right ($3569).
build_outline's half count.
Builds shape A's fill, 64 bytes from $6B80 + A x 64, into sprites $64 and $65 at $5900: two halves of five blank rows and sixteen of two bytes ($35DB).
The byte after build_fill's RTS: 0, read by nothing.
Clears five rows of a sprite pair at ($25) and ($27), then copies 16 rows of four bytes from ($23), three to the left sprite and one to the right with the rest cleared.
Skips five rows of a sprite at ($25), then copies 16 rows of two bytes from ($23).
A random byte: the next byte of page $1F (the LDA operand's low byte steps) EOR the interrupt count.
random's LDA operand, low byte: the step through page $1F.
Shows message A ($3635) and waits until it has been typed.
Starts message A on the bottom row: the old one scrolls off first; $FF scrolls it off and types nothing.

Once a frame: every two frames scrolls the old message two characters left (19 times), then types the new one a character at a time with the cursor ($27) after it; letters are ASCII less $34, a space blank.
show_message's scroll count ($36D5), stage ($36D6: 0 scrolling, 1 typing, 2 done), nothing-to-type flag ($36D7), column ($36D8), frame delay ($36D9) and a done flag nothing reads ($36DA).
The message's stage: 0 scrolling, 1 typing, 2 done.
Nothing to type: $FF for message $FF.
The column being typed.
The frames to the next step.
Set to $FF when a message is done; nothing reads it.

Reads the three fire buttons: the up-arrow key (keyboard row 6, column 6), joystick one's fire and joystick two's fire. Returns carry set and A = 0, 1 or 2 for the first one held, carry clear when none is.
The runner's device: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.

Reads the runner's device: joystick one or two as the port reads, or the keyboard as a joystick: @ up, : down, H left, K right and the up-arrow key fire, a 0 bit for each held. The manual gives K as left and H as right.
Joystick two.
read_controls's work byte.
Waits X frames.
Waits for the raster to pass line 256: the bottom of the screen.
Blanks the clock's cells, rows 2 to 4 from column 20, and their colours.
Marks the pill's sprites to be taken off. Not reached.
Colours the four parts of the panel's icon (its top, its two sides, its middle and its foot) from the table at $37DD for the current set.
The icon's four colours for each set, four bytes a set.
The Flyer's icon colours, then the Runner's, the Burrower's, the Jumper's and out of energy's.
Draws the top panel, rows 0 to 7, from the 320 bytes at $382B.
The top panel's characters, eight rows of 40: the power and course box on the left, the energy box, the clock box and the forms' icon box.
Panel row 1.
Panel row 2. The clock's box and the icon's top.
Panel row 3.
Panel row 4.
Panel row 5.
Panel row 6.
Panel row 7.
Not called: prints A and the address X, Y in hex at $4102, a debugging aid left in.
debug_hex's address operand, low byte.
debug_hex's address operand, high byte.
debug_hex's second LDA, from the address + 1.
Its operand's low byte.
debug_hex's second operand, high byte.
Not called: prints X and Y in hex as well.
debug_regs's A at the first place.
Not called: prints A as two hex digits.
Not called: prints one hex digit as a character.
The LDA operand debug_digit writes through: the screen place, from $4102.
Not called: prints X in hex at the third place.
Not called: prints Y in hex at the fourth place.
Nonzero once an effect has been started: 1 in the load, and nothing in this part changes it.
Each voice's script finished: 1 when it has.
Voice 2's script finished.
Voice 3's script finished.
Not called: silences the SID ($3E1C) with A, X and Y saved.
When every voice's script has finished, silences the SID.
Plays effect 0, whose table entries are $0000; reached only while $39DC is 0, which it never is here.
Starts effect A on voices 1 and 2: their script pointers and marks from $3AB6 and $3AD0, their tick counts and note lengths reset. Ignored while one is starting.
play_effect's effect number.
1 while an effect starts.
Starts effect A on voice 3 alone, from $3AEA, for the landing (1), the hurt (2) and the next screen (12), which then sound over voices 1 and 2.
play_effect3's effect number.
The effects' scripts, an address a voice: voice 1's ($3AB6), voice 2's ($3AD0), voice 3's ($3AEA), numbered from 0.
Voice 1's script addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Voice 2's table.
Voice 2's script addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Voice 3's table.
Voice 3's script addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
Addresses of the 23 instruments, numbered from 1.
The instrument addresses' high bytes, interleaved.
The instruments, seven bytes each: attack/decay, sustain/release, waveform, pitch slide low and high, slide rate, and a vibrato byte.
Instrument 2: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $B0, waveform $20, slide $0000 at rate 0, vibrato 0.
Instrument 3: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $70, waveform $80, slide $0100 at rate 3, vibrato 6.
Instrument 4: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0, waveform $80, slide $FE00 at rate 0, vibrato 0.
Instrument 5: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $FA, waveform $80, slide $0010 at rate 0, vibrato 0.
Instrument 6: attack/decay $00, sustain/release $F0, waveform $80, slide $0200 at rate 0, vibrato 0.
